stem: The horizontal surface below the bigger block M is smooth. A small block A (mass m) rests on top of M and is joined by a light string over a light pulley at M's top-right corner to a second small block B (mass m) hanging in contact with M's vertical right face (see figure). The coefficient of friction between the blocks is μ. The maximum horizontal force F which can be applied to M to keep the smaller blocks at rest with respect to the bigger block is (a) ((1 − μ)/(1 + μ))(M + m)g (b) ((1 + μ)/(1 − μ))(M + m)g (c) ((1 + μ)/(1 − μ))(M + 2m)g (d) (1 + μ)(M + 2m)g

Passage (Q5–Q7): A system of masses is shown in the figure with masses and coefficients of friction indicated: block A (20 kg) rests on block B (30 kg), which rests on block C (40 kg), which rests on the ground; μ between A and B = 0.1, between B and C = 0.2, between C and ground = 0.1. A horizontal force F is applied to block B. (g = 10 m/s²) Q7. The minimum value of F for which A slips on B is (a) 125 N (b) 150 N (c) 175 N (d) 180 N

Passage (Q6 & Q7): A monkey of mass m clings to a rope hanging over a fixed pulley at the edge of a horizontal table. The opposite end of the rope is tied to a weight of mass M lying on the table. The coefficient of friction between the weight and the table is μ. The monkey moves downwards w.r.t. the rope with an acceleration b. Q7. The tension of the rope is (a) Mm(μg + g + b)/(M + m) (b) Mm(μg − g + b)/(M + m) (c) Mm(μg + g − b)/(M + m) (d) Mm(μg − g − b)/(M + m)

A given object takes n times the time to slide down a 45° rough inclined plane as it takes to slide down an identical perfectly smooth 45° inclined plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface of the inclined plane is (a) √(1 − 1/n²) (b) 1 − n² (c) 1 − 1/n² (d) √(1 − n²)

A block of mass 1 kg is pushed up a surface inclined at 60° to the horizontal by a force of 10 N parallel to the inclined surface, with μ s = 0.1. When the block is pushed up by 10 m along the inclined surface, the work done against frictional force is (g = 10 m s⁻²): (a) 5√3 J (b) 5 J (c) 5 × 10³ J (d) 10 J

Consider a block kept on an inclined plane (inclined at 45°). If the force required to just push it up the incline is 2 times the force required to just prevent it from sliding down, the coefficient of friction between the block and inclined plane (μ) is equal to: (a) 0.33 (b) 0.60 (c) 0.25 (d) 0.50

A uniform chain of 6 m length is placed on a table such that a part of its length is hanging over the edge of the table. The system is at rest. The coefficient of static friction between the chain and the surface of the table is 0.5. The maximum length of the chain hanging from the table is ___ m.
